- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model may lag in adjusting downward; apply early correction to avoid prolonged overestimation.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when price deviates >3σ from 18-day moving average; model often fails to revert; force correction toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- In sentiment-neutral periods (sentiment ≈0.00), model tends to drift toward recent highs; apply downward bias to avoid overconfidence in continuation.
- If sentiment is high and price is falling, model often ignores sentiment; force upward adjustment to reflect market sentiment shift.
